value.rationale: Strong two-window phase retrieval is a natural measurement question that requires one window by itself to determine each signal. The full ten-site problem lies exactly beyond previously known composite sufficient bandwidth and the closest period-five sector threshold; solving its complete joint Fourier support obstruction produces the sharp universally sufficient bandwidth 3 and an explicit failing signal at 2. The 10-point case is a natural first composite-order benchmark, not an arbitrarily selected unmotivated subfamily.
